correctness.rationale: In the repaired active class, empty sites remain ON, and on the triangle every occupied OFF can activate because it has an empty ON neighbor. All-ON configurations communicate by alternating hops with activation; choosing hop destinations realizes all five phase/occupation types and their relabelings. Independently constructed and solved the exact five-state lumped chains. The only rate difference is the escape rate from the split state with both occupied clocks OFF, 2c versus c. With escape rate αc, collision mass is (c+1)(c+2) divided by (c+1)(c+2)+2/α+4c+2c². This yields both stated stationary laws for all c>0 and the positive factorized gap, tending to 1/6 at zero and decaying as 1/(9c²). With all clocks initially ON, there is at most one OFF site when there is one particle (OFF implies occupied) or when there are only two sites (every hop leaves an ON source). Hence all eligible neighbors are ON in the smaller cases. The repair excludes all-OFF absorbing states rather than asserting they do not exist. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_triangle_seasons.py, output /workspace/branches/triangle_seasons_reproduction.txt.
residual_risks: The identified stationary law of the gated process is not a statement about arbitrary stationary mixtures on the unrestricted phase space.

value.rationale: The repaired finite boundary case pinpoints when the solvable neighbor-gated surrogate first changes a natural stationary observable, holding all hopping and reset rules fixed. The all-rate sign and distinct slow- and fast-clock scales distinguish physical neighbor gating from an artifact of an arbitrarily chosen absorbing start. This is a useful exact benchmark even without a general-size inequality.
residual_risks: No claim about the sign for more particles, other topologies or thermodynamic condensation.
